step.body: We audit your existing pipeline, data sources, and query patterns to determine whether your bottleneck is retrieval quality, context utilization, or cost-per-query. We also benchmark your current latency and accuracy to establish a baseline.

We implement the chosen architecture in milestones: retrieval and indexing first for RAG, prompt compaction and context management for long-context, then orchestration, caching, and guardrails.

faq-item.faq-q: Is RAG cheaper than long-context windows in 2026?
faq-item.faq-a: At scale, yes. RAG typically costs 10-100x less per query because it only sends relevant chunks to the model, while long-context models charge for every token in the prompt—even irrelevant ones. For low-volume, high-complexity queries, long-context may be more cost-effective despite higher per-query cost.

faq-item.faq-q: When does long-context beat RAG on accuracy?
faq-item.faq-a: Long-context wins when the answer requires synthesizing information across many documents or when retrieval fails due to ambiguous queries. However, with good chunking and reranking, RAG often matches or exceeds long-context accuracy at a fraction of the cost.

faq-item.faq-q: How do I handle data freshness with long-context models?
faq-item.faq-a: Long-context models are static—they only know what's in the prompt. For fresh data, you either need to inject updated context into every prompt (expensive) or use RAG to retrieve the latest information from a live source. Most production systems in 2026 use a hybrid: long-context for reasoning, RAG for freshness.

faq-item.faq-q: Can I use both RAG and long-context in one system?
faq-item.faq-a: Yes, and that's the recommended pattern. Use RAG to fetch relevant chunks, then use a long-context model to reason over them together with your instructions. This gives you the cost savings of retrieval with the synthesis power of long-context models.

faq-item.faq-q: What does it cost to build a RAG or long-context system?
faq-item.faq-a: A free architecture assessment is available. Full RAG builds range from $8,000 to $30,000+, long-context optimization from $5,000 to $20,000, and hybrid systems from $15,000 to $40,000+, depending on complexity and data volume. Contact for a fixed-price quote.
